title: The Paris Agreement and Global Governance

walkthroughs.body_html: The UNFCCC of 1992 established the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities'. The Kyoto Protocol of 1997 set binding targets for Annex I (developed) countries but excluded major emerging emitters, contributing to the US withdrawal and Canada's later exit.

The Paris Agreement (12 December 2015) introduced a bottom-up architecture: every country submits NDCs covering mitigation and (optionally) adaptation. The agreement commits to limiting warming to 'well below 2 °C' and 'pursuing efforts' for 1.5 °C, with five-yearly stocktakes encouraging ratchets in ambition.

Current NDCs still imply warming of around 2.5-2.9 °C by 2100. Climate finance commitments — particularly the $100 billion/year pledge to developing countries — have been slow to materialise. COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022) agreed to establish a loss and damage fund; subsequent COPs are negotiating its operationalisation.
